correctness.rationale: Reconstructed full proof. Step 1 establishes P=conv of class cubes and its down-closed max-gauge description. Step 2 classifies every F vertex by active tight-edge rank (integral stable sets or 0/1/2 vectors across at least three parts). Step 3 uses strict coordinatewise residual reduction to prove the all-half vector is uniquely farthest, even among nonvertices. Step 4 solves the strictly convex blockwise projection with KKT, including clipping, uniqueness, r=3 reciprocal formula. Step 5 proves strict discrete balancing via concavity and uniqueness of minimizers; extreme profiles have an exact interior solution and correct fixed-r asymptotics. Step 6 checks the four-class phase boundary exactly. Independent finite-graph halfspace enumeration, numerical projections, and exact-rational size-profile tests passed. No infinite assertion relies solely on finite experiments.

The prior cube-to-stable-set metric statement maximizes over the entire cube, which is not the fractional edge polytope F; a maximal cube vertex can dominate while the half vertex is the unique maximizer in the present problem.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The two admissible optimization orders are distinct: prior minimum-enclosing-sphere uses min over centers then max over integral vertices, and cube approximation uses max over cube points then min over P, while the new result uses max over F then min over P. None implies the exact r-partite clipped formula or the four-class contact transition.

value.rationale: The intrinsic geometric precision of an important edge-inequality LP relaxation is a motivated unknown invariant. A complete arbitrary-profile formula, unique deepest fractional point, contact-set phase change, exact r=3 harmonic law and balanced-to-concentrated scale separation are not routine relabelings or negligible numerical refinements; they distinguish different relaxation qualities at identical graph order and part count.
